sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: Hungarian often marks the possessor relationship directly on the possessed noun — either as a suffix attached to it, or as a stand-alone possessive pronoun built the same way.

Enyém ('mine') isn't a suffix stuck onto a noun — it's a free-standing word that replaces the noun-plus-suffix combination when you don't need to repeat the object: az autó az enyém instead of az autó az autóm. English does something similar with 'mine' versus 'my car'; Hungarian just has a dedicated pronoun for every person.
